---
title: "Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors"
description: "An original worked mathematical lesson corresponding to MML §4.2."
---

**Reference:** *Mathematics for Machine Learning*, Chapter 4, §4.2. The teaching example and explanation here are original.

## Why we need this concept

A transformation may preserve certain directions, only stretching or flipping them. These are eigenvectors, while the stretch factors are eigenvalues.

## Derive the structure

$$
A\boldsymbol v=\lambda\boldsymbol v,\qquad \det(A-\lambda I)=0
$$

Check the shapes and conditions in this statement before applying it. The formula encodes the exact relationship to reason about, rather than replacing a derivation with a library call.

## Worked example

For A=diag(2,3), the directions (1,0) and (0,1) remain on their own axes, scaled by 2 and 3. Its characteristic polynomial is (2-lambda)(3-lambda), yielding eigenvalues 2 and 3.

## Interpretation and limitations

Eigenvalues need not be real for arbitrary real matrices. Symmetric covariance matrices have real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors; that is why they work naturally in PCA.

## Challenge

Does (1,1) satisfy the eigenvector relation for diag(2,3)? Check each component.
